extracted.intended_audience: teachers, educational theorists, and education policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical principles and evaluative criteria for education generally, with emphasis on democratic social conditions — what education should aim to do, how subject-matter and heredity should be treated, and what social arrangements promote educative experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heredity as original endowment
rubrics_metrics.description: For educational purposes heredity means neither more nor less than the original endowment of an individual. Education must take the being as he is; that a particular individual has just such and such an equipment of native activities is a basic fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful study of native aptitudes and deficiencies is a preliminary necessity, but the educator's task is to furnish an environment which will adequately function whatever activities are present. Do not attempt by instruction to make of an individual something for which he is not naturally fitted; yet recognize that original capacities are often more varied and potential than presently utilized. (Illustration: language requires native vocal/auditory equipment plus an environment of speakers to select and coordinate activity.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment selects and coordinates activity (heredity–environment relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of native equipment in no way guarantees that an individual will attain particular capacities; the environment in which activities occur settles what is developed (e.g., a child with vocal organs will not develop speech in a 'dumb unsocial environment').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educators must provide environments that activate and select native tendencies. The presence of requisite faculties is necessary but not sufficient; instruction should focus on creating conditions that make desired activities meaningful and likely to be adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter should serve present processes, not glorify the past
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper subject matter of instruction is to keep the process alive; the study of past culture-products is valuable only when it enters into and serves the present. Making records and remains of the past the main material of education cuts the vital connection between present and past and makes the past a rival of the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical/cultural materials as resources that increase the meaning of present activity rather than as ends in themselves. Avoid treating culture as mere ornament, refuge, or asylum; integrate past products so they direct and enrich current problems and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as continuous reconstruction of experience (technical definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is that reconstruction or reorganization of experience which adds to the meaning of experience, and which increases ability to direct the course of subsequent experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat educative process and educative end as unified: learning is the transformation of quality of experience. Every continuous activity that reveals previously imperceptible connections and produces a disposition toward things possessing meaning is educative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increment of meaning: perception of connections and continuities
rubrics_metrics.description: The increment of meaning corresponds to the increased perception of the connections and continuities of the activities in which we are engaged (e.g., through action one learns connections between sight, touch, and heat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiences that make connections perceptible rather than presenting isolated rules or answers. Instruction should lead learners to see bearings and relationships so that actions become intelligible, not mere tricks producing correct answers without understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in power to direct subsequent experience (anticipation and control)
rubrics_metrics.description: A genuine educative experience increases ability to anticipate consequences, prepare in advance, secure beneficial outcomes, and avert undesirable ones — i.e., to intend consequences rather than merely letting them happen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate learning by its impact on a learner’s capacity to plan and control future behavior. Favor experiences that cultivate foresight and purposeful action over those that merely train automatic routine skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of capricious and merely routine activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuinely educative experiences are distinct from capricious activity (acting without perceiving consequences) and from routine action (automatic skill that does not reveal new bearings). Capricious activity stems from maladjustment; routine action may increase skill but narrows the meaning-horizon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer instruction away from tasks where pupils cannot see the connection between method and result. Provide activities that reveal consequences and relations; discourage rote tasks that produce mechanical competence without expanded understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should be social as well as personal (social reconstruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconstruction of experience may be social as well as personal: in progressive communities education can be used consciously to shape young people so that future society will be an improvement on the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design schooling to promote habits and interactions that intentionally reconstruct social life for improvement, not merely to reproduce existing customs. Education’s remit includes formation of future society through shared experiences and social aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for worth of social life: variety and reciprocity of shared interests
rubrics_metrics.description: To measure the worth of a mode of social life ask: How numerous and varied are the interests which are consciously shared? How full and free is the interplay with other forms of association?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational ends and methods should be evaluated by how well they produce many shared interests and free interchange. Partial or narrow common interests produce partial and distorted socialization; wide reciprocity promotes balanced development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of isolation and exclusiveness in social groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation of a group (families, nations, schools, classes) brings rigidity, formal institutionalizing, and selfish ideals; lack of free equitable intercourse prevents social endosmosis and leads to distorted culture and intellectual imbalance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote interaction across groups (home–school–community links, cross-class contacts). Avoid educational practices that seclude schools or communities from broader social intercourse, since isolation fosters static habits and narrows mental life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic ideal for education: accessibility, initiative, and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: A democratic community requires intellectual opportunities accessible to all on equable and easy terms and educates for personal initiative and adaptability so members can respond to varied and changing shared interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess educational systems for equity of access and for how well they cultivate initiative and adaptability. In mobile, intercommunicating societies, prioritize education that prepares citizens to perceive connections, take initiative, and adjust to change rather than produce a narrowly trained elite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject fixed-class sorting; recognize individual uniqueness and indefinite capacities
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should not be limited to testing and assigning individuals to a few fixed classes of capacities (Plato's model). Original capacities are indefinitely numerous and variable; social organization in a democracy should utilize specific and variable qualities of individuals rather than stratify by classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid educational systems that rigidly classify students into a small number of types or destinies. Favor flexible, diagnostic, and developmental approaches that discover diverse aptitudes and permit varied trajectories rather than static occupational sorting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should reveal relations in work and motivate beyond mechanical skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency and scientific management reduced to purely technical externals produce narrowed intelligence; workers require understanding of the relations of a man to his work—including relations to others—to enlist intelligent interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula and workplace education should teach the technical, intellectual, and social relationships involved in work so individuals engage because of perceived significance, not merely for pay or routine. This broadens motivation and prevents sterile specialization.
